hints.formula: Speed = distance ÷ time, so rearrange to make time the subject.
hints.subs: Use metres for distance and metres per second for speed.
hints.answer: Divide the distance by the speed.
hints.unit: Time in SI units is measured in seconds.

hints.formula: First find the weight W = mg, then share it equally between the legs.
hints.subs: g is 9.8 m/s² (10 m/s² is also accepted). Count the legs touching the ground.
hints.answer: Multiply mass by g, then divide by the number of legs.
hints.unit: Load is a force, so it is measured in newtons.

stride-distance.name: Distance from motor speed and stride

hints.formula: Number of rotations = f × t. Each rotation moves the robot one stride.
hints.subs: Convert mm to m (divide by 1000) and minutes to seconds (multiply by 60).
hints.unit: You converted the stride to metres, so the answer is in metres.

hints.formula: Angular velocity is angle turned per unit time, with the angle in radians.
hints.subs: Convert degrees to radians: multiply by π and divide by 180. You can type pi, for example pi/6.
hints.answer: Divide the angle in radians by the time.

hints.formula: Arc length travelled = θ × r. Speed = arc length ÷ time.
hints.subs: Convert the angle to radians (180° = π) and the radius to metres (50 cm = 0.5 m).
hints.answer: Multiply θ by r, then divide by t.
hints.unit: Linear speed is in metres per second.

spin-turn.name: Wheel rotations in a spin turn

vars.label: wheel radius r (same unit as R)

hints.formula: Each wheel travels an arc (θ/360) × 2πR. One rotation of the wheel covers 2πr. Divide and the 2π cancels.
hints.subs: In a spin turn the robot turns about its centre, so R is HALF the wheel spacing. Use the same unit for R and r.
hints.unit: The answer is a number of rotations (revolutions).

at-rest.name: When is the robot at rest?

hints.formula: At rest means velocity is zero. Velocity is the derivative of position.
hints.subs: Differentiate each term: d/dt of kt³ is 3kt², of kt² is 2kt, of kt is k, of a constant is 0. Write v = at² + bt + c.
hints.answer: Solve at² + bt + c = 0 by factorising or the quadratic formula. There are two times.

hints.formula: The formula is given in the question: lift starts at 0 when θ = 0.
hints.subs: Keep θ in degrees if your calculator is in degree mode. cos 90° = 0.
hints.answer: Work out 1 − cos θ first, then multiply by r.
hints.unit: r was in centimetres, so the lift is in centimetres.

problems.question: An autonomous delivery vehicle moves at 0.5 m/s. How long does it take to travel 10 m?
A four-legged walking robot has a mass of 8 kg. Calculate the load on each leg when it stands on all four legs. (g = 9.8 m/s²)
A crank motor turns at 0.5 rev/s and the walking robot moves 80 mm per rotation. How far does it travel in 3 minutes?
A robot joint rotates 30° in 0.25 s. Find its average angular velocity in rad/s.
A robot wheel of radius 50 cm rotates through 180° in 5 s. Find its linear speed in m/s.
A two-wheel differential robot has wheel radius 20 cm and wheel spacing 30 cm. It makes a 72° spin turn. How many rotations does each wheel make?
A robot's position is P(t) = 2t³ − 9t² + 12t + 5. At what times is it momentarily at rest?
problems.working: v = dP/dt = 6t² − 18t + 12 = 6(t − 1)(t − 2) = 0, so t = 1 s and t = 2 s.

problems.question: An eccentric cam with eccentricity r = 4 cm rotates through 90°. Using s = r(1 − cos θ), find the follower lift.
